To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of rice, corn and soy flour to wheat flour at 10,10 and 10%, respectively, resulted in acceptable and nutritious breads.
addition of rice, corn and soy flour to durum wheat flour can be used up to 20%, while in bread wheat flour it can be used up 10% without any negative effect on bread making and sensory properties.
rice, corn, or soy flours up to a level 10% can be incorporated into wheat flour to produce bread with acceptable quality and reasonable acceptability by consumers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of bread with improved nutritional value and acceptable eating quality.
the development of breads from different wheat varieties enriched with different levels of rice, corn and soy flour.
the development of breads with improved nutritional quality and reduced production costs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the incorporation of 10% rice flour, corn flour, and soy flour in bread wheat flour and 20% of these nongluten flour in durum wheat flour can be recommended for the production of nutritious bread with acceptable quality characteristics.
rice, corn and soy flours could be incorporated into the bread and durum wheat flour at 10% level to produce acceptable bread without any negative impact on the quality characteristics.

bread wheat and durum wheat flurs can be substituted with rice, corn, or soy flours up to the 10% level without any negative effects in quality attributes and reasonable acceptability offering promising nutritious and health alternative to consumer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bread wheat flour can be substituted by rice, corn and soy flour up to 10%, while durum wheat flour can be replaced by the same flours up to a level 20% without significant changes in the quality of the bread.
rice and corn flours can be used in the bread and durum wheat flour to improve its protein content, lysine, fiber, and minerals.
rice, corn, soy flour can be used to substitute wheat flour up to certain level in bread making without any negative effect on the quality of the bread.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rice, corn, or soy flour can be added up to 10-20% level in wheat flour to produce bread with acceptable quality and nutritional characteristics.
the use of nongluten flour in the production of wheat-based foods can provide a healthy alternative for consumers and a reduction in the cost of production of bread.
